 Judgment
This is the complaint instituted by the complainant against the accused under section 200 of Cr.P.C.
for the offence punishable under section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act1881.
2. The averments of

the complainant in brief is as follows:
The complainant is a company incorporated under the provisions of Companies Act,
1956 and licensed by the Reserve Bank of India.

Further the complainant company is involved in the business of providing financial facilities for purchase of motor vehicle as per SCCH-10 the terms and conditions of the loan agreement and having registered office at the address mentioned in the cause title above and branch at Bengaluru.

Further it is submitted by the complainant that, the accused had approached the complainant company for financial assistance of Rs.2,61,000/ for procuring a MARUTI OMNI STD 5STR vehicle bearing registration No.KA21 N 4220 and entered into an loan agreement bearing No.2371108 and the accused had agreed abide the terms and conditions of the agreement.
Further the accused became chronic defaulter in payment of loan amount.

Further on several demands and notices, towards the due amount accused had issued a cheque bearing No.208161,
dated 20022020 for a sum of Rs.2,90,000/ drawn on Corporation Bank,
Nellayadi Branch.

The said cheque was presented by the complainant through its banker HSBC Bank, M.G.Road Branch, Bangalore but the same has been returned with SCCH-10 an endorsement as "Funds Insufficient" as per the bankers memo dated 29022020.

Then, the complainant got issued a legal notice to the accused dated 1803 2020 demanding the payment of the cheque amount by RPAD and calling upon the accused to pay the cheque amount within 15 days from the date of receipt of the said notice and the said notice was returned unserved as Not claimed on 04042020.
Therefore, the accused has committed an offence punishable U/Sec.138 and Sec.142 of Negotiable Instrument Act.
Hence, the complainant prayed to punish the accused U/Sec.138 of N.I.Act and award compensation to the complainant.
3. After filing of the complaint, the cognizance of the offence was taken and registered criminal case against the accused and the summons was issued to him.
Upon service of the summons, the accused had appeared before the court through his counsel and was enlarged on bail.
Subsequently, plea was recorded and SCCH-10 the substances of the accusation was read over and explained to accused.
He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried, then the case was posted for complainant evidence.

4. In view of judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Indian Bank Association and others V/s. Union of India and others, the sworn statement on affidavit is treated as evidence of complainant and it is considered as Pw1 evidence and documents are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6.

sentences.text: Further, the Statement of the Accused U/Sec.313 of Cr.P.C was recorded and incriminating circumstances appeared in the evidence against the accused were read over to the accused and accused denied the all incriminating circumstance appeared in SCCH-10 the evidence.
Then the case was set down for defence evidence.
In spite of sufficient time the accused has not lead defence evidence.
6. Heard the arguments from both counsel and I have perused the records.

7. Now the points that would arise for my consideration are as follows:
1. Whether the complainant proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused had issued a cheque bearing No.208161 dated 20022020 for a sum of Rs.2,90,000/ drawn on Corporation Bank, Nellayadi Branch for discharge of legal debt and when the said cheque was presented to the Bank for encashment it was returned unpaid with remarks that "Funds Insufficient" and inspite of service of demand notice the accused has not paid the amount and thereby committed SCCH-10 an offence punishable under section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act?
2.
What order?

8. On the basis of the materials available on records, my findings to the above points are as follows:
POINT NO.1: In the Negative.

POINT NO.2: As per the final order for the following:
REASONS 09. POINT No.1: The Complainant has filed this complaint alleging that the accused has committed offence punishable under section 138 of N.I. Act.

He pleads and asserts that, the accused has approached the complainant company and seeking for financial assistant of Rs.2,61,000/ for procuring Maruthi Omni STD 5STR vehicle bearing reg.No.KA21N4220 and entered into loan agreement No.2371108 and accused agreed to abide by the terms and conditions of the agreement and agreed to repay the loan amount by monthly installments.
SCCH-10
Further the accused become a chronic defaulter in payment of installment.

Therefore the complainant requested to accused to repay the loan due amount, on request the accused issued the cheque bearing No.208161 dated 20022020 for a sum of Rs.2,19,000/ drawn on Corporation Bank Nellaydi Branch towards due amount.
The complainant has presented the said cheque for encashment through its banker.
The said cheque was returned unpaid with an endorsement "Funds Insufficient" as per memo 29022020.
Thereafter, the complainant has got issued legal notice on 18032020 to the accused by demanding the payment of cheque amount and it was returned as not claimed on 04042020.
In spite of notice, the accused has failed to pay the cheque amount.

Therefore, the accused committed an offence under Section 138 of N.I.Act.

3 SCCH-10 10.

sentences.text: To substantiate his case, the G.P.A. Holders of the complainant company have got examined themselves as PW.1 and PW.2 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 respectively.

The PW1 and PW2 have reiterated the contents of the complaint in their affidavit evidence about lending of loan,
issuance of cheque by the accused towards discharge of his liability and its dishonour for "Funds Insufficient" and issued the legal notice to the accused calling upon him to pay the amount covered under cheque and his failure to comply the same.
11. In this scenario, let me scrutinize the documents relied by complainant in order to examine the compliance of statutory requirements envisaged under section 138 of N.I. Act.
Ex.P.1 is the General Power of Attorney, Ex.P.2 is the cheque and it bears signature as per Ex.P.2(a)
, the said cheque was returned with an endorsement "Funds Insufficient" as per Ex.P.3 bank SCCH-10 endorsement dated 29022020.

Ex.P.4 is legal notice dated 18032020, Ex.P.5 is Postal receipt and Ex.P.6 is the unserved postal cover, Ex.P.6(a) is the copy of legal notice, Ex.P.7 is the General Power of Attorney,
Ex.P.8 is the loan agreement, Ex.P.9 is the recall notice and Ex.P.10 is the statement of account.
12. The counsel for the complainant argued that, the accused has issued the cheque for discharge his liability and the same has been dishonor.
Therefore the complainant has complied the statutory requirements, therefore the presumption U/Sec.118 and 139 of NI Act shall be drawn in favour of complainant.

The Sec.118 and 139 of N.I. Act are read as follows: The Section 118 reads as here: 
"That every negotiable instrument was made or drawn for consideration and that every such instrument when it has been accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred SCCH-10 was accepted,
endorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration".
Further Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act provides for presumption in favour of a holder.

It reads as here:  "It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque, of the nature referred to in section 138, for the discharge, in whole or in part, or any debt or other liability."
A combined reading of above said sections raises a presumption in favour of the holder of the cheque that he has received the same for discharge in whole or in part of any debt or other liability.
13. No doubt, the said presumptions of law are rebuttable in nature.
The accused can take probable defence in the scale of preponderance of probability to rebut the presumption available to the complainant.
Let me examine whether the accused has successfully rebutted the said presumptions of law.
In this back SCCH-10 ground, this court has given anxious consideration to the materials available on record.
14. The accused contended that, there is no legally recoverable debt and the complainant has misused the security cheques issued by him at the time of loan.
Further contended that, the PW2 has no power to give evidence.
The claim of the complainant is time barred claim, therefore the accused is liable to be acquitted.

sentences.text: To prove the said fact, the accused counsel has crossexamined the PW2, the PW2 has admitted in his crossexamination that: "It is true that, loan term was completed in the year 2016.
We have issued the notice to the accused in the year 2016 for repayment of due amount.
I have not produced the said notice copy."
The Pw2 clearly admitted that the loan term completed in the year 2016.
The complainant has issued SCCH-10 the notice for repayment of due amount in the year 2016 itself.
The complainant produced legal notice as per Ex.P.4 dated 18032020 and recall notice dated 0906 2016 as per Ex.P.9.
The complainant has issued the notice on 09062016 demanding the due amount and thereafter the complainant has not taken any steps.
16. The counsel for the accused contended that, the claim of the complainant is time barred debt.
Admittedly the demand notice is issued on 09062016.
Thereafter the present complaint filed based on disputed cheque by issuing the legal notice on 18032020 which is beyond limitation.
The complainant counsel argued that the accused has issued the cheque by admitting his due.
Further argued that, the accused has not disputed the cheque and signature.
Therefore the accused is liable to be convicted.
SCCH-10

The counsel for the accused has relied the decisions:
1. Criminal Appeal No.20057/2016 (The Bidar Urban Cooperative Bank Ltd., V/s. Mr.Girish)
2. Criminal Appeal No.1028/2010 (Shriram Transport Finance Co.Ltd., V/s. Smt. Asamabi Shabhan)

entities.text: Bidar Urban Cooperative Bank Ltd., V/s. Mr.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Shriram Transport Finance Co.Ltd., V/s. Smt. Asamabi Shabhan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In these two decisions the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that the time barred debt is not legally enforceable or recoverable debt under section 138 of N.I.Act except specific written acknowledgement of debt.
Further held that mere issuance of cheque without corresponding legally enforceable debt is not an offence.
17. In the present case the complainant/Pw2 has admitted in his crossexamination that the loan term was completed in the year 2016 and notice issued in the year 2016 as per Ex.P.9.
Since Ex.P.9 the complainant has not taken any steps for recovery of the loan amount.
SCCH-10

The cheque alleged to be issued on 20022020 it is beyond limitation from Ex.P.9,
therefore the claim of the complainant based on disputed cheque is time barred debt.

Hence,
Sec.138 is not attracted to the time barred debt.
In this case the Pw2 has admitted in his cross examination that: "It is true that, I have not produced documents to show as on 20022020 the due was Rs.2,90,000/."
The complainant has produced the loan agreement, loan account statement as per Ex.P.8 and 10.

The Pw2 stated in his crossexamination that, the account statement as per Ex.P.10 discloses the due amount of Rs.2,92,610/ and the Pw2 denied that, there is a difference in the account statement and cheque.
On carefully perusal of Ex.P.10 i.e., account statement does not disclose the due amount either Rs.2,92,610/ nor cheque amount Rs.2,90,000/.
The account statement SCCH-10 not at all discloses the cheque amount i.e. sum of Rs.2,90,000/ as on the date of issuance of cheque.

sentences.text: In this case, the counsel for the accused has disputed the competency of evidence given by the PW2 dated 12102022 and submitted that the GPA of the PW2 as per Ex.P.7 is expired on 01 102022.

The GPA of PW2 as per Ex.P.7 clearly discloses that, "this Power of Attorney shall stands automatically terminated on 01 102022" the same is admitted by the PW2 in his cross examination on 12102022.
19.

The counsel for the accused has relied the decision in Criminal Revision Petition No.129/2013 (George Joseph and another V/s. HMT (International) Limited and another).
In this case

entities.text: George Joseph and another V/s. HMT (International) Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the Hon'ble High Court held
that ,

the proceedings are held to be vitiated want of authority to prosecute the complainant on behalf of company by the power of attorney holder without having proper SCCH-10 authorization or GPA executed by Chairman or other officers of the company without a delegation of power to institute such proceedings having emanated from the Board of Directors would invalidate any proceedings brought without a necessity authority.

20. In this case, the Pw2 has given evidence on 12102022 which is after termination of GPA,
therefore the evidence of the Pw2 is not reliable which is deposed on 12102022.

It is pertinent to note that, the complaint filed by the complainant is not at all maintainable in view of claim is barred by limitation and also the complainant failed to show the cheque amount is legally enforceable debt and the same is due as on the date of issuance of cheque, because the account statement as per Ex.P.10 does not disclose the due amount.
Therefore, I am of the opinion that, the complainant has failed to prove the guilt of the accused as the accused has issued the SCCH-10 cheque for legally enforceable debt or liability.
Therefore the accused is liable to be acquitted.
Hence, I answer the point No.1 in the Negative.
21. POINT NO.2:
In view of the reasons stated and discussed above, the complainant has failed to prove the guilt of the accused for the offence punishable under section 138 of N.I. Act.
Hence, I proceed to pass the following: ORDER Acting Under Sec.255(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is hereby acquitted for the offence punishable U/sec.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act.
The bail bond shall stand cancelled.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, typed by her and corrected by me and then pronounced in the open court on 21st day of February 2023)
